> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/services/service-record-context/package.json`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **1** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **69** of **252** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **183** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **183**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **124** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **0** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 58570d8002dd213f7f65525d881ac935583f4050` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `1b5162a9cf2d320c2424ff7b79307e70b47646c5` — the merge of head `007615908a5a15466ef2ae3724885d009e8fb213` into base `58570d8002dd213f7f65525d881ac935583f4050`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 1b5162a9cf2d320c2424ff7b79307e70b47646c5 && git checkout 1b5162a9cf2d320c2424ff7b79307e70b47646c5
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 58570d8002dd213f7f65525d881ac935583f4050 007615908a5a15466ef2ae3724885d009e8fb213 && git checkout -B drift-repro 58570d8002dd213f7f65525d881ac935583f4050 && git merge --no-ff 007615908a5a15466ef2ae3724885d009e8fb213

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 58570d8002dd213f7f65525d881ac935583f4050
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 58570d8002dd213f7f65525d881ac935583f4050` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `TIER_DEFAULT`
Head-sha: `32aba545983608ea7b5787ffeb82d95c829267e2`
Local-runs: none

PR #37550, card #37463. Read: the card and its six comments (os-dev report 7192952275, amendment 7192997436), the PR body, the net diff (7 files), and the head's check-runs (53 completed: 37 success, 16 skipped, 0 failed). Code outside the diff was read, not run.

### ① Derived judgments

- **Accept set: unchanged. Right.** No call that answered before is refused now, and none that was refused answers now. Only the error answer of a failing read moves.
- **One classifier at four sites. Right.** `isCodedRefusal` (non-empty string `code` and a declared 4xx, `.status` then `.statusCode`) is the verifier's old private `isRefusal`, moved unchanged. `refusedOrFailed` calls it at the exposure check, the served-definition read, `publishedOf` and the child list query. It is not on the package entry (`src/index.ts`), so no export is added.
- **Coded refusals unchanged. Right.** The refusals the two real doors throw at these reads all declare a status: `OBJECT_API_DISABLED` 404, `OBJECT_API_METHOD_NOT_ALLOWED` 405, `OBJECT_PACKAGE_DISABLED` 404, `PermissionDeniedError` 403. The stdio door's `FIELD_VISIBILITY_UNRESOLVED` 503 moves from 403 to 503, which is correct for a read that could not be evaluated.
- **The 503 leaks nothing. Right.** Both MCP doors answer a coded 5xx through `mapDataError`'s declared-5xx arm: code and status kept, sentence replaced by `Internal server error`. That arm is reached before any arm that reads `cause`, and the arms before it are keyed on other codes. No stack, path, driver text or child name reaches the wire. The executor's own sentence names the pack and the root only, inside ADR-0160 D4's naming bound.
- **No ADR-0160 amendment owed. Right.** D4 "The naming bound" and point 12 fix one code for "every such refusal"; D3 "Object level" covers gates that refuse. No sentence of ADR-0160 speaks of a read that fails. ADR untouched, as the claim fences.
- **Callers.** An AI caller on either door reads `SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE` 503 for an outage and `PERMISSION_DENIED` 403 for a refusal, so the two are told apart. The verifier drops and reports the first, drops and stays silent on the second. Right, subject to the findings below.
- **Pins.** Each of the four sites has its own uncoded-throw case, and its own coded-refusal control. The verifier pin and one real-kernel case on both doors are present. One ablation was run, on the classifier (every throw read as a refusal): 16 service cases and the harness case failed. The opposite direction (a refusal read as a failure) was not ablated; the per-site controls cover it.

**M1 (must-fix) — at both MCP doors the outage is logged once, at `warn`, as a "declared capability absence", and the original error is never logged.** `dataDoorErrorResult` (`packages/mcp/src/mcp-http-tools.ts`) hands `logServerFault` the door's `code`. `SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE` with a 5xx is on `CAPABILITY_ABSENCE_CODES` (`packages/types/src/server-fault-log.ts`), the list for "this deployment did not install that". Such a line is printed once per route per process (the route is `tools/call get_record_context` plus the root object), at `warn`, without the error object, so without `cause`. Every later outage on that root object prints nothing. On `main` the child list query's raw throw was logged at `error` on every call with the driver's text; this PR takes that away. The card names the people who debug outages as a beneficiary, and the changeset says the original error is there "for the host". That holds for the verifier's `onError` only. Fix either by a failure code that is not on the absence list, or by logging the cause at `error` in the door (that file is outside the claimed surface, so it needs a claim amendment). Pin the log line in the harness case. Read from the three functions; not run.

**S1 (should-fix) — the `readFailed` sentence reaches no MCP caller.** The doors withhold a 5xx sentence unless the throw declares it for the caller (`refusal: true`, or `userMessage`). The throw declares neither, so the caller reads `Internal server error`. The en and zh-Hans sentences, the locale test, and the advice "try again later, or read the record with get_record" are in-process only. The changeset reads as if the caller is shown the sentence. Either declare it for the caller and pin it on both doors, or say in the changeset what the doors answer.

**S2 (should-fix) — at the child list query, a refusal the door recognises without code-plus-status is now answered as an outage.** On `main` that throw was not caught, so the door classified it. A sandboxed `beforeFind` hook's plain `throw new Error(...)` (no `code`) answered 400 `HOOK_ABORTED` with the hook's sentence; a code-only `PERMISSION_DENIED` answered 403. Both now answer 503 `Internal server error`. The card's wording ("not a coded refusal") and the verifier's rule support the dev's line, so this needs a decision, not a guess: either ask the door's classification at this one site, or rule that a status-less refusal is a failure here and pin it. The query control uses a coded 403 only.

**N1 (nit)** — the changeset says all four reads were refused `PERMISSION_DENIED` 403 before. The child list query was not: it answered the door's 500 (the dev's own reading). The PR body's table has it right.

**N2 (nit)** — every uncoded throw is `SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE`, a bug included. The error catalog gives that code `retry_backoff`, so a deterministic bug invites retries. The card allows the code.

### ② Semver level

- `patch` on `@objectstack/service-record-context`: right. A bug fix, no new entry export, no spec change. `SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE` 503 is already in the error ledger and the error catalog. The `packages/runtime` change is a test, so it publishes nothing.
- `Clause-②: no`: right, with no arm. Not a widening: nothing new is accepted. Not a narrowing: nothing accepted before is refused now. No published type, protocol doc or skill documents 403 for a failed read; `skills/objectstack-ai/references/context-packs.md` states 403 for a related object nobody is served, which still holds.
- `Metadata-protocol: none`: right. Both lines are line-initial in the PR body and the changeset. `Check Changeset` passed.

### ③ Boundary flags

- `open_questions`: none filed.
- Deviation 1 (`verify-citations.ts` edited): answered by claim amendment 7192997436. Accepted.
- Deviation 2 (the child query's coded refusal is rethrown as the door wrote it): accepted for coded refusals, as on `main`. The status-less case is S2, escalated to the area.
- Deviations 3 and 4 (PR footer, a killed waiter): process only, no contract effect.
- SQL push-down: no new read, no id materialisation, no in-app join. The diff wraps the one existing child query in a `try`.
- No `packages/spec/**` and no `docs/adr/**` in the diff, as the claim fences.

## 席位核对

Head-sha: `32aba545983608ea7b5787ffeb82d95c829267e2`
**REWORK** — L1, seat repo:objectstack#5

1. **Shape**: open draft against `main`, `Fixes #37463`. 7 files, +255/−54. Not governed. `Clause-②: no`, `Metadata-protocol: none`, patch; the reviewer confirms this, since no published surface documents the old answer. No review face, so the declaration face applies; the seat ran it on the contract-review tier because it changes an error answer.
2. **Premise**: one classifier, `isCodedRefusal`, now runs at all four sites. Coded refusals are unchanged, and an uncoded throw answers 503 `SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE` without leaking anything. No ADR-0160 amendment is needed.
3. **Gates**: contract record 7193179486 reads **FAIL**, with one must-fix. CI on this head: 37 success, 16 skipped, 0 failed.
4. **Owed for the delta**:
   - **M1**: the outage now disappears from the server log. `SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE` with a 5xx is on `CAPABILITY_ABSENCE_CODES` (`packages/types/src/server-fault-log.ts`). So `dataDoorErrorResult` logs it once per root object per process, at `warn`, as a capability absence, without the error or its `cause`; on `main` it was logged at `error` on every call. Make an outage log at `error` with its cause on every occurrence. Either answer with a failure code that is not on the capability-absence list, or log the cause in the door. If the fix touches a file outside the claim, amend the claim first. Pin it, with the ablation.
   - **S1**: the en and zh-Hans `readFailed` sentences and the "try again later, or use get_record" advice never reach an MCP caller, because both doors replace an undeclared 5xx sentence with `Internal server error`. Either make the changeset and PR body say what the caller actually sees, or carry the sentence to the caller. The seat prefers the first; it is cheaper and honest.
   - **S2**: the seat rules here. A child-query throw that `main` already answered as a refusal stays a refusal. That means a sandboxed `beforeFind` hook's plain throw keeps 400 `HOOK_ABORTED`, and a code-only `PERMISSION_DENIED` keeps 403. Only a truly uncoded failure becomes 503. Pin both cases.
   - N1 (the changeset misstates the child query's old answer): fix it with S1. N2 (a bug also reads as a retryable 503) is accepted.
5. **Out of scope and where it went**: none.
6. **Next**: push, then knock. The same reviewer reads M1, S1 and S2. After ACCEPT, area ai-36996 lands it.

Delta review of PR #37550 (card #37463) against my record on `32aba545`. Read: the diff between the two heads, the net diff against `main` (9 files), REWORK 7193191377, claim amendment 7193352452, rework report 7195114149, the PR body, and the new head's check-runs (73 completed: 62 success, 11 skipped, 0 failed). Code outside the diff was read, not run.

### ① Derived judgments

Prior findings:

- **M1: closed.** A failure now throws `INTERNAL_ERROR` 500, which is not on `CAPABILITY_ABSENCE_CODES`, so `logServerFault` prints it at `error` on every call. The fault line prints no `cause`, so the failure's stack ends in `Caused by:` plus the original's stack. The harness pins four `[5xx] 500` error lines (two doors, two calls), each with the outage in its stack, and no capability-absence warning. The ablation back to `SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE` fails at that pin. The stack is not on the wire: the same case asserts no outage text in either door's answer.
- **S1: closed.** The changeset and PR body now say an MCP caller reads `INTERNAL_ERROR` 500 with `Internal server error`, and that the `readFailed` sentence is in-process only.
- **S2: closed**, as the seat ruled. The child list query asks `mapDataError`; a throw the door answers below 500 is rethrown as the same object. A sandboxed `beforeFind` plain throw stays 400 `HOOK_ABORTED` in the hook's words and a status-less `PERMISSION_DENIED` stays `PERMISSION_DENIED`, pinned in the unit suite and on both doors, each with a control. The ablation back to `isCodedRefusal` fails all four. The three object-level sites keep `isCodedRefusal`, where `main` answered 403 for every throw, so nothing regresses there.
- **N1: closed.** The changeset no longer says the child query answered 403.
- **N2: accepted by the seat** (REWORK 7193191377). Not re-graded.

Check 1, the `@objectstack/types` dependency: right.

- Graph: `@objectstack/types` depends on `@objectstack/spec` only, so no cycle. `@objectstack/core`, already a dependency here, depends on it, so no new package enters the closure. Ten sibling services already depend on it. It is a published package.
- Lockfile: the importer stanza for `packages/services/service-record-context` gains the three lines that match the manifest (`workspace:*`, `link:../../types`); nothing else in the lock moved.
- Surface: claim amendment 7193352452 covers `package.json` and the lock stanza.

Check 2, what `mapDataError` reclassifies at the child list query:

- Below 500: nothing. The throw is rethrown untouched and the door classifies it as it did on `main`.
- At 500 and above: every answer becomes `INTERNAL_ERROR` 500. Finding S3.

**S3 (should-fix) — at the child list query, a fault the door answered with its own code is now `INTERNAL_ERROR` 500.** On `main` the raw throw reached the door, which answered `ERR_DATASOURCE_UNAVAILABLE` as 503 with its sanitised sentence, a driver errno as `DATABASE_ERROR` 500, a driver's declared `NOT_IMPLEMENTED` 501 as 501, and a declared 5xx with `refusal: true` or `userMessage` with its sentence. All of these now read `INTERNAL_ERROR` 500 `Internal server error`. The caller loses the retry signal of a 503 and the datasource sentence. This is still a failure, names nothing, is logged, and the verifier reports it either way, so it does not block. But the seat's S2 ruling said only a truly uncoded failure takes the failure code, and the changeset says the doors answered this read `INTERNAL_ERROR` (500) before, which is true for an uncoded throw only. The seat decides: rethrow a fault the door answers with a code other than `INTERNAL_ERROR`, or keep one code and say so in the changeset. No pin covers a coded fault at this site; the "coded 5xx" case runs at the served-definition read.

**N3 (nit)** — the predicate asks `mapDataError` with the child's name; the door asks with the root's. One arm of the classifier (a message that quotes the object's name beside "not", answered 404) depends on that name. Where the two disagree, the result is either the door's answer as on `main`, or a 500 where `main` answered 404 for an uncoded driver message. Rare, and no refusal a producer declares is affected.

Unchanged from the first record and still right: the accept set, the classifier at the object-level sites, no leak in the 5xx answer (`mapDataError`'s fault arms do not render the message or `cause`), no ADR-0160 amendment owed.

### ② Semver level

- `patch` on `@objectstack/service-record-context`: right. A new dependency on a sibling already in the closure adds no export and needs no higher level. The changeset names the dependency. `Check Changeset` passed.
- `Clause-②: no`, no arm: right, for the first record's reasons. `INTERNAL_ERROR` 500 is in the error ledger.
- `Metadata-protocol: none`: right. Both lines are line-initial in the PR body and the changeset.

### ③ Boundary flags

- `open_questions`: none filed.
- Deviation 1 (the cause carried on the stack, not fixed in the fault log): accepted. It stays inside the claim, and the platform-wide gap is filed as #37598.
- Deviation 2 (S2 applied at the child list query only): accepted; it is what the seat ruled.
- Deviations 3 and 4 (PR body rewritten through the relay, one gate rerun): process only.
- SQL push-down: no new read, no id materialisation, no in-app join.
- No `packages/spec/**` and no `docs/adr/**` in the diff.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `TIER_DEFAULT`
Head-sha: `007615908a5a15466ef2ae3724885d009e8fb213`
Local-runs: none

Second delta review of PR #37550 (card #37463) against my record on `bd03a37e`. Read: the diff between the two heads (5 files), the net diff against `main` (9 files), REWORK 7195238190, rework report 7197010507, the PR body, and the new head's check-runs (73 completed: 62 success, 11 skipped, 0 failed). Code outside the diff was read, not run.

### ① Derived judgments

- **S3: closed.** The child list query now asks `doorAnswersItself`, which reads `mapDataError` and nothing else. A throw the door answers with a code or sentence of its own is rethrown as the same object, so the caller reads what `main` answered: `ERR_DATASOURCE_UNAVAILABLE` 503 with its sentence, `DATABASE_ERROR` 500, a driver's `NOT_IMPLEMENTED` 501, a declared 5xx with its sentence or `userMessage`. Only an uncoded failure becomes `INTERNAL_ERROR` 500. Five unit cases pin the coded faults, each first asserting the door's own answer; four controls at the same site pin the uncoded side. The harness pins `ERR_DATASOURCE_UNAVAILABLE` 503 with its sentence on both doors, one `[5xx] 503` log line per door, and a control. The ablation back to the previous predicate fails those six cases. The changeset now says `INTERNAL_ERROR` (500) applies to an uncoded failure only and lists what the door keeps answering.
- **M1, S1, S2, N1: stay closed.** This delta does not touch the failure's code, its log line, the refusal rethrow or the object-level sites. N2 and N3 stay accepted by the seat.

The check asked for, whether "the door's anonymous answer" is detected robustly: yes.

- The test is three conditions on the door's own answer: status exactly 500, `error` equal to `INTERNAL_ERROR_MESSAGE` (the constant the door itself writes, imported, not a copied string), and no body key other than `error` and `code: 'INTERNAL_ERROR'`.
- A coded `INTERNAL_ERROR` 500 with a real sentence is not swallowed. If the producer declares the sentence for the caller (`refusal: true`), the door's `error` is that sentence, so the throw is rethrown. If it declares a `userMessage`, the body carries that key, so it is rethrown. If it declares neither, the door itself withholds the sentence and answers `Internal server error`; the wrapped failure puts the same bytes on the wire, and the original sentence is on `cause` and in the logged stack.
- A demoted code (`declaredCode` in the body), a 500 under any other code, and any status other than 500 (a status-only 503 included) all count as the door's own answer and are rethrown.
- It fails safe. If the door ever adds a key to its anonymous answer, the throw is rethrown and the door answers it as on `main`; the four unit controls would then fail and show the drift.

No new finding.

### ② Semver level

- `patch` on `@objectstack/service-record-context`: right, unchanged. `doorAnswersItself` is exported from the module, not from the package entry, so no export is added. No manifest or lockfile change in this delta. `Check Changeset` passed.
- `Clause-②: no`, no arm, and `Metadata-protocol: none`: right, both line-initial in the PR body and the changeset.
